prompt_text: I need a new air conditioner installed in Atlanta. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I just need one quick detail: what ZIP code or neighborhood in Atlanta is the install for, and is this a single-family home, townhome, or commercial space? With a ZIP I can pull the best local, highly rated installers and their contact details. 

While you reply, here are three reputable companies that commonly serve the Atlanta area and why you should call them, plus exactly what to ask each company when you get quotes.

Recommended companies to call (Metro Atlanta)
- Coolray Heating & Air Conditioning
  - Why: Long-established regional company with a large local presence, lots of techs for timely installs and service, handles major brands and offers emergency/after-hours support.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (Metro Atlanta franchise)
  - Why: National brand with local franchise service and broad resources for parts/backups; typically good for warranty follow-through and multiple service trucks.
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (Atlanta franchisees)
  - Why: Franchise network that emphasizes on-time installs and guarantees; good option for scheduling and customer service-driven installations.

Why these kinds of companies
- Regional firms (like Coolray) have deep local experience with Atlanta homes and HVAC sizing for our climate.
- National franchises (ARS, One Hour) have standardized training, parts supply, and warranty systems that reduce risk if something goes wrong.
- For best results, you should also include at least one strong independent local licensed dealer who is a factory-authorized dealer for the brand you prefer (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Goodman, etc.). Factory dealers can offer better equipment warranties and factory-trained installers.

What to ask every company when you call
1. Are you licensed in Georgia and insured? Ask for license number and insurance proof.  
2. Do you have NATE-certified technicians?  
3. Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and show me the results? (This determines correct unit size.)  
4. Which brand and model are you proposing, and what is the SEER rating?  
5. What is included in the written estimate (equipment, labor, permit fees, refrigerant type, ductwork changes, thermostat, line set, condensate drain)?  
6. What are the equipment and labor warranties (length, who services claims)?  
7. Can you provide references from recent local installations?  
8. What is the approximate install timeline, and will you handle permits and final inspections?  
9. Do you offer financing or rebates, and can you help with utility rebates/credits?  
10. Will you provide a written price breakdown and a firm total?

How to proceed
- Get at least three written quotes (same scope), including one from a factory-authorized dealer for your preferred brand.  
- Verify license & insurance, read recent Google/Yelp/BBB reviews, and check references.  
- Compare apples-to-apples: same SEER, same ductwork work, same permit handling.  
- Don’t accept a quoted “tonnage” only—ensure they show a Manual J and show match to recommended indoor coil and airflow.

If you want, give me your ZIP code and whether this is a house or commercial install and I’ll pull 3–5 top-rated local contractors (with phone numbers and links to reviews) so you can call them directly.
